mainTopic: Did the first holiness of ירושלים last forever? רבי יצחק on בית חוניו, his retraction, and the search for תנאים who argue about it
overview: This amud opens with the last line of the משנה: after שילה was destroyed, people could again bring קרבנות on private altars (במות), but after ירושלים was destroyed, they could not. רבי יצחק reports that קרבנות are brought in בית חוניו in Egypt even today. The גמרא says this rests on two ideas: בית חוניו is not עבודה זרה, and the first holiness of ירושלים was only for its time. It supports this with a פסוק that compares נחלה (ירושלים) to מנוחה (שילה). רבי יצחק later denies saying it, but רבא swears he did, so he must have taken it back because of רב מרי's challenge from two משניות. The גמרא then searches for תנאים who argue about whether the first holiness lasts forever. It first tries רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע, but רבינא shows they may agree. It then turns to רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי on the walled cities, but a second ברייתא in his name seems to contradict the first. The amud ends by asking why the returning exiles needed to consecrate the cities at all, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the משנה: שילה versus ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends by contrasting the holiness of שילה with the holiness of ירושלים: after שילה there is permission, but after ירושלים there is none.
steps.simpleTranslation: [After the holiness of שילה ended] there is permission, but after the holiness of ירושלים there is no permission.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line of the משנה. It says that once שילה was destroyed, private altars became allowed again, but once ירושלים was destroyed, they did not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'there is permission after it' refer to bringing קרבנות on a במה (private altar) after the main sanctuary is gone. The משנה claims ירושלים is different: its holiness keeps the ban on במות in place even after the חורבן. The גמרא is about to bring a view that seems to go against this.

keyTerms.meaning: Permission; here, permission to bring קרבנות on private altars
The city where the משכן stood before the בית המקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the rule the whole following גמרא is testing: does the holiness of ירושלים really last after the חורבן?

phrases.english: After it there is permission,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the holiness of שילה from earlier in the משנה. After it, people could bring קרבנות on private altars.

phrases.english: but the holiness of Jerusalem: after it there is no permission.

steps.triggerLanguage: יֵשׁ אַחֲרֶיהָ הֶיתֵּר, וּקְדוּשַּׁת יְרוּשָׁלַיִם אֵין אַחֲרֶיהָ הֶיתֵּר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After שילה, private altars are allowed again. After ירושלים, they remain forbidden.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: קרבנות are offered in בית חוניו today
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with רבי יצחק, who says he heard that people bring קרבנות in בית חוניו even nowadays.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי יצחק said: I heard that people bring קרבנות in בית חוניו at the present time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a surprising report from רבי יצחק: קרבנות are being brought in בית חוניו, a temple in Egypt, in his own day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If bringing קרבנות outside the בית המקדש is allowed today, that seems to clash with the משנה, which says that after ירושלים there is no permission. The גמרא will next explain what this view must be based on.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
The temple of חוניו (Onias), built in Egypt

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יצחק is not asking a question here. He is reporting a practice he heard about. The reasoning behind it comes in the next step.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rabbi Yitzchak said:
I heard that they offer sacrifices in the temple of Onias
phrases.notes: בית חוניו was a temple in Egypt, set up as a copy of the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: at the present time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק שָׁמַעְתִּי שֶׁמַּקְרִיבִין בְּבֵית חוֹנְיוֹ בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a view that seems to go against the משנה's rule that there is no permission after ירושלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קרבנות are brought in בית חוניו nowadays.

steps.title: The two assumptions behind רבי יצחק's report
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יצחק holds two things: בית חוניו is not a place of עבודה זרה, and the first holiness of ירושלים was only for its time.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that בית חוניו is not a house of עבודה זרה. He also holds that the first holiness made ירושלים holy only for its time, and not for the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning that would allow קרבנות in בית חוניו. It names two separate assumptions, and both are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Assumption one: the קרבנות there are brought to ה׳ and not to idols. Assumption two: the first holiness of ירושלים was only for its time, so once the בית המקדש was destroyed, the ban on bringing קרבנות elsewhere ended too. Put together, these mean that a temple outside ירושלים would be allowed today.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds / is of the opinion
The first holiness, given in the time of the first בית המקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: The question of קדושה ראשונה קידשה לשעתה is a famous מחלוקת. It affects the status of ירושלים and the הר הבית after the חורבן.

phrases.english: He holds: the temple of Onias
is not a house of idol worship,
and he holds: the first holiness —
phrases.notes: This is the holiness ירושלים received in the days of the first בית המקדש.

phrases.english: sanctified it for its time
and did not sanctify it for the future.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר בֵּית חוֹנְיוֹ לָאו בֵּית עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי יצחק's report.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two requirements: בית חוניו is not עבודה זרה, and קדושה ראשונה was only לשעתה.

steps.title: The פסוק links ירושלים to שילה
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק places מנוחה (שילה) next to נחלה (ירושלים). Just as there was permission after שילה, there is permission after ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'For you have not yet come to the rest and to the inheritance.' 'Rest' is שילה, and 'inheritance' is ירושלים. The פסוק compares inheritance to rest: just as after 'rest' there is permission, so too after 'inheritance' there is permission.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a פסוק as the source for the idea that the holiness of ירושלים was only for its time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions מנוחה and נחלה together, and this is read as a היקש (a comparison drawn from two things placed side by side). Everyone agrees that after שילה was destroyed, במות became allowed. So the same should be true after ירושלים was destroyed, which goes directly against the משנה's line.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares by placing side by side (היקש)

steps.whatToRemember: The view that allows בית חוניו rests on reading 'מנוחה and נחלה' as a היקש: ירושלים is just like שילה, so its holiness also ended when it was destroyed.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'For you have not yet come
phrases.notes: This פסוק is in דברים (12:9). משה is speaking to the people before they enter the land.

phrases.english: to the rest and to the inheritance.'
'Rest': this is Shiloh,
'Inheritance': this is Jerusalem,
it compares inheritance to rest:
just as after 'rest' there is permission,
so too after 'inheritance' there is permission.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב כִּי לֹא בָּאתֶם עַד עָתָּה אֶל הַמְּנוּחָה וְאֶל הַנַּחֲלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the idea that קדושה ראשונה was only לשעתה.
steps.raayaObject: That the holiness of ירושלים ended with its destruction, just as שילה's did.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 12:9, read as a היקש between מנוחה (שילה) and נחלה (ירושלים).

steps.title: The Sages ask רבי יצחק whether he said it
steps.stepSummary: The Sages ask רבי יצחק directly: did you really say this?
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Did you say this?
steps.whatsHappening: The other Sages go back to רבי יצחק and ask him to confirm that he said this about בית חוניו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is startling, so the Sages want to check whether it is really his. This sets up his answer in the next step.

phrases.english: They said to him: Did you say it?
phrases.notes: 'It' means the statement about bringing קרבנות in בית חוניו.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the statement in step 2 is really רבי יצחק's.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יצחק actually made the statement about בית חוניו.

steps.title: רבי יצחק answers: No
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק tells them he did not say it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: No.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק denies that he said that קרבנות are brought in בית חוניו today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His denial seems to take away the whole statement and the reasoning built on it. The next step will challenge this denial.

phrases.english: He said to them: No.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He says he did not say it.

steps.title: רבא swears that רבי יצחק did say it
steps.stepSummary: רבא swears that רבי יצחק did say this ruling, and that רבא himself learned it from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: By God! He said it, and I learned it from him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא strongly insists, using an oath, that רבי יצחק really did say this ruling, because רבא heard it from him in person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's testimony goes against רבי יצחק's denial. The result is that he did once say it, but later took it back. So the ruling is on record as his, even though he no longer stands behind it.
steps.whatToRemember: The ruling about בית חוניו was really said by רבי יצחק, and רבא learned it from him. רבי יצחק later denied it, which means he took it back.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not calling רבי יצחק a liar. He is confirming that the ruling was once said, which shows that רבי יצחק later took it back.

phrases.english: Rava said: By God!
He said it,
and I learned it from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רָבָא הָאֱלֹהִים אַמְרַהּ וּגְמִירְנָא לַהּ מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes against רבי יצחק's denial in step 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יצחק did say the ruling about בית חוניו, and רבא learned it from him. His later denial shows that he took it back.

steps.title: Why did he take back his ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יצחק denied his own ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason he went back on his ruling?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא just swore that רבי יצחק really did say this ruling, so now the גמרא asks why רבי יצחק later denied it. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יצחק once said it and later denied it, he must have changed his mind. The גמרא wants to know what made him retract.

keyTerms.meaning: He went back on it; he retracted

phrases.english: And what is the reason he retracted?
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי יצחק. רבא proved he said it, so his "I didn't say it" means he changed his mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רבא's oath that רבי יצחק did say the ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason רבי יצחק retracted his ruling about בית חוניו and ירושלים's holiness.

steps.title: Because of רב מרי's challenge
steps.stepSummary: He retracted because of a difficulty raised by רב מרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the difficulty of רב מרי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יצחק changed his mind because of a challenge from רב מרי. The next step spells out what that challenge was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This short line only names the source of the retraction. The content of the challenge comes right after.

phrases.english: Because of the difficulty of Rav Mari.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יצחק retracted because of רב מרי's challenge.

steps.title: רב מרי's challenge from two משניות
steps.stepSummary: Two משניות show that after ירושלים there is never again permission to offer on private altars. So ירושלים's holiness is permanent.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב מרי objected: the holiness of שילה has permission after it; the holiness of ירושלים has no permission after it. And we also learned: once they came to ירושלים, the private altars became forbidden and they never again had permission, and it was the 'נחלה'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי quotes two משניות saying that after ירושלים was chosen, private altars (במות) were forbidden forever. That goes against רבי יצחק's idea that ירושלים's first holiness was only for its time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק compared ירושלים to שילה: after each, במות became allowed again. The משנה says the opposite: שילה had permission after it, but ירושלים did not. So ירושלים's holiness never ended, and רבי יצחק's comparison falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: The holiness of the משכן's location at שילה
Permission (here: to offer on private altars)
Private or improvised altars outside the משכן or מקדש
The inheritance, meaning ירושלים, the permanent resting place

steps.confusionAlert: "Permission after" means permission to bring קרבנות on private altars after the place was destroyed. It is not talking about some other kind of permission.

phrases.english: As Rav Mari objected:
The sanctity of Shiloh: there is permission after it.
phrases.notes: After the משכן at שילה was destroyed, people were allowed to bring קרבנות on private altars again.

phrases.english: The sanctity of Jerusalem: there is no permission after it.
And furthermore, we learned in a mishna:
Once they came to Jerusalem, the improvised altars were prohibited,
and they no longer had permission,
and it was the inheritance.
phrases.notes: This is the same "נחלה" from the פסוק in step 4. The משנה reads it as the permanent place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the challenge named in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's view that ירושלים's first holiness was only for its time, and his comparison of ירושלים to שילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two משניות state outright that after ירושלים there was never again permission for במות. That means its holiness is permanent, which contradicts רבי יצחק.

steps.title: This is a dispute of תנאים: רבי אליעזר on the curtains
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the question is a תנאים dispute and brings רבי אליעזר's tradition about curtains during the building of the second מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute of תנאים. As it is taught: רבי אליעזר said, I heard that when they were building the היכל, they made curtains for the היכל and curtains for the עזרה. The only difference was that for the היכל they built from outside, and for the עזרה they built from inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that רבי יצחק's view does have support, because תנאים argued about this very question. It starts by quoting רבי אליעזר, setting up a contrast with רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר reports that temporary curtains were put up while the second מקדש was being built. The גמרא will soon read this as a sign that, in his view, the walls (or curtains) were needed because the old holiness had lapsed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
Curtains or hangings used as temporary walls
The Sanctuary building of the מקדש

phrases.english: It is a dispute of tanna'im.
(As it is taught:) Rabbi Eliezer said:
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets ("as it is taught").

phrases.english: I heard that when they were building the Sanctuary,
they made hangings for the Sanctuary and hangings for the courtyard.
Except that for the Sanctuary they built from outside,
phrases.notes: The workers built the היכל walls standing outside the curtains, without going in.

phrases.english: and for the courtyard they built from inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּאֵי הִיא דְּתַנְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב מרי's challenge, the גמרא shows רבי יצחק's view matches one side of a תנאים dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The question is a תנאים dispute; רבי אליעזר reports that curtains were set up for the היכל and the עזרה during rebuilding.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: the holiness lasts forever
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says קרבנות may be brought and eaten even without walls, because the first holiness was forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע said: I heard that we offer even with no Temple building, we eat קדשי קדשים even with no curtains, and קדשים קלים and מעשר שני even with no city wall, because the first holiness sanctified for its time and sanctified for the future.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע gives the other side: no building, curtains or wall is needed, because the first holiness never ended. This clearly states the 'forever' view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע ties his rulings to one reason: the first holiness was for its time and also for the future. Since he says this openly, it sets up the גמרא's next step of figuring out what רבי אליעזר must hold.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of the most holy level, eaten in the עזרה
Offerings of lesser holiness, eaten in ירושלים

steps.whyThisMatters: Whether the first holiness of ירושלים and the מקדש lasts forever is a basic question with big practical effects for the Temple Mount today.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua said:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁמַעְתִּי שֶׁמַּקְרִיבִין אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בַּיִת,
phrases.english: I heard that one sacrifices even though there is no Temple,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹכְלִין קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין קְלָעִים,
phrases.english: one eats offerings of the most sacred order even though there are no hangings,

phrases.aramaic: קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין חוֹמָה,
phrases.english: and offerings of lesser sanctity and second tithe even though there is no wall,
phrases.notes: The word "eats" from the line before carries over here.

phrases.english: because the first sanctity sanctified for its time
and sanctified for the future.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second half of the same teaching (a משנה in עדיות), contrasting with רבי אליעזר.
steps.raayaObject: That the question of permanent holiness is debated by תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע's statement that the first holiness sanctified for the future.

steps.title: So רבי אליעזר holds it was not forever
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יהושע needed to say 'forever', רבי אליעזר must disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: By implication, רבי אליעזר holds that it did not sanctify for the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that רבי אליעזר disagrees with רבי יהושע and holds the holiness was not forever. That would make רבי יצחק follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning: רבי אליעזר needed curtains, which suggests the old holiness had lapsed, while רבי יהושע said none were needed because the holiness is forever. So there seems to be a real מחלוקת, and רבי יצחק has a תנא to rely on.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication; from this we learn

phrases.english: By inference, Rabbi Eliezer holds:
It did not sanctify for the future.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the contrast between steps 11 and 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אליעזר holds the first holiness was not forever, so the question is a תנאים dispute.

steps.title: רבינא: maybe both agree, and each told what he heard
steps.stepSummary: רבינא suggests both תנאים hold the holiness is forever; each just reported a different tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: From where do you know? Perhaps everyone holds the first holiness sanctified for its time and for the future, and one Sage said what he heard, and the other Sage said what he heard.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges the inference that רבי אליעזר disagrees. Maybe both agree the holiness is forever, and they simply reported different facts they had heard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים open with 'שמעתי', 'I heard'. So רבי אליעזר may only be reporting that curtains were used, not taking a stand that holiness lapsed. If so, there is no real מחלוקת.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
From where do you know this?
Perhaps everyone agrees that
the first sanctity sanctified for its time
and sanctified for the future,
and this Sage said what he heard,
phrases.notes: This one is רבי אליעזר, who heard about the curtains.

phrases.english: and that Sage said what he heard.
phrases.notes: This one is רבי יהושע, who heard they offered without walls.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי מִמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference made in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבי אליעזר holds the holiness was not forever.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both statements are 'I heard' reports of different facts, so no disagreement can be inferred.

steps.title: Then why did רבי אליעזר need curtains?
steps.stepSummary: If the holiness never ended, why were curtains needed at all according to רבי אליעזר?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: according to רבי אליעזר, why do I need curtains?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא raises a possible objection to his own suggestion: if holiness never lapsed, the curtains seem pointless. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole inference in step 13 rested on the curtains, which looked like they were needed to make the area holy. This question tests whether רבינא's reading can explain them.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (an expected objection)

phrases.english: And if you would say:
Why do I need hangings according to Rabbi Eliezer?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא קְלָעִים לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An anticipated objection to רבינא's suggestion in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's claim that רבי אליעזר also holds the holiness is forever.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If holiness never ended, curtains would serve no purpose, yet רבי אליעזר reports they were made.

steps.title: The curtains were only for privacy
steps.stepSummary: The curtains were just for modesty and privacy, not to create holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: Merely for privacy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers that the curtains were only there for privacy, so the holy service would not be on display to everyone. So they prove nothing about whether the holiness lapsed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This removes the basis for saying רבי אליעזר disagrees. The curtains had a practical, respectful purpose, not a holiness purpose, so both תנאים can hold the holiness is forever.
steps.whatToRemember: רב מרי showed from משניות that ירושלים's holiness is permanent, which is why רבי יצחק retracted. The גמרא tried to find a תנא who holds it was not forever, but רבינא showed both רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע may agree it is forever. The curtains were only for privacy.

phrases.english: Merely for privacy.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the purpose of the curtains
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The curtains were needed to make the area holy, which would show רבי אליעזר holds the holiness lapsed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The curtains were only for privacy, so רבי אליעזר can agree the first holiness lasts forever.

steps.title: A תנא who says the first holiness ended
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי says the first walled cities lost their holiness when the Land was lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this question is argued about by other תנאים. A ברייתא says that רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי asked why the חכמים listed only these particular walled cities. He answered that when the exiles came back from בבל, they found these cities and made them holy again. The first walled cities had lost their holiness when the Jewish people were exiled from the Land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is looking for a real argument among תנאים about whether the first holiness was forever. It brings a ברייתא where one תנא says the old walled cities lost their status in the exile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא's suggestion removed the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. So the גמרא needs another source that clearly says the first holiness ended. רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי's words 'the first ones were nullified' supply exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: תנאים, the sages of the משנה era
The exiles who returned from בבל
They were nullified, meaning they lost their status

phrases.english: Rather, it is like these tannaim,
as it is taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei, said:
Why did the Sages list these?
phrases.notes: 'These' means the short list of walled cities in a משנה in ערכין. There were surely many more walled cities than that.

phrases.english: Because when the exiles came up
they found these and consecrated them,
but the first ones were nullified
phrases.notes: 'The first ones' are the walled cities from the time of יהושע.

phrases.english: once the land was nullified.
phrases.notes: He means once the Jewish people were exiled and stopped living in the Land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since רבינא made the first pair of תנאים agree, the גמרא offers a different pair of תנאים who do argue.
steps.raayaObject: That some תנאים hold the first holiness was only temporary.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי: 'the first ones were nullified once the land was nullified.'

steps.title: So he holds the first holiness was only for its time
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא, the גמרא concludes that רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי holds the first holiness lasted only for its own time.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it seems he holds that the first holiness made the place holy only for its own time, and not for the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the ברייתא it just quoted: this תנא holds the first holiness was not forever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the old cities could lose their status in the exile, then their holiness was never permanent. That places רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי on the side of 'for its time only.' This is the opposite of רבי יהושע's view of 'forever.'

keyTerms.meaning: The first holiness, from the time of יהושע and the first בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי (in the first ברייתא) holds the first holiness was only for its time. The old walled cities lost their status in the exile, and עזרא's returnees had to make them holy again.

phrases.english: Apparently he holds:
the first holiness sanctified for its time
and did not sanctify for the future.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the general principle from the ברייתא in step 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי holds the first holiness was temporary.

steps.title: A second version of the same תנא's words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another ברייתא from רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי that does not say the old cities lost their holiness. This seems to contradict the first ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But another ברייתא contradicts this. רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי said: Were these really the only walled cities? The פסוק says there were sixty cities in the region of ארגוב, and it says all of them were fortified with high walls. So why did the חכמים list only these? Because when the exiles came back, they found these and consecrated them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different ברייתא with the same תנא's words, and this version seems to clash with the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version he stresses that many walled cities existed, but he never says the old ones lost their status. That suggests the others were still holy and simply were not identified, which would mean the first holiness lasted. So the same תנא now seems to hold both 'for its time' and 'forever.'

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted it, raising a contradiction
The region of ארגוב, on the east side of the ירדן

steps.confusionAlert: Both ברייתות are said by the same person, רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי. The problem is not two sages arguing. It is one sage who seems to say two different things.

phrases.english: And they contrasted it:
Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei, said:
Were these the only ones?
Wasn't it already stated:
"Sixty cities, all the region of Argov,"
phrases.notes: This פסוק is in דברים, about the cities of עוג that משה conquered.

phrases.english: and it is written:
"All these were cities fortified with a high wall."

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָמָּה מָנוּ חֲכָמִים אֶת אֵלּוּ?
phrases.english: Rather, why did the Sages list these?
Because when the exiles came up
they found these and consecrated them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי from steps 17–18 by quoting another version of his words.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי holds the first holiness was only for its time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second version does not say the old cities lost their status, and it stresses that many walled cities existed. This implies their holiness continued, which contradicts the first version.

steps.title: Why consecrate them if they were still holy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the word 'they consecrated them' in the second ברייתא. If the holiness never ended, no new consecration would be needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: They consecrated them?! If they were still holy, why would they need to consecrate them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem inside the second ברייתא itself. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second ברייתא suggests the old holiness lasted. But it still says the returnees 'consecrated' the cities, which only makes sense if the holiness had ended. The גמרא will need to explain what that word really means.

keyTerms.meaning: They consecrated them, meaning they made them holy

phrases.english: They consecrated them?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Zooms in on one word of the ברייתא from step 19 that does not fit how the גמרא is reading it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'קידשום' in the second ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the second ברייתא holds the first holiness lasted, then a new consecration is pointless. So the word 'consecrated' does not fit.
